findings.where: The logo, wherever it appears: the hero mark, and the nav lockup (mark plus 'MMM INFRA') on desktop and phone
findings.fault: The logo has been recoloured. The arches are drawn in the palette's near-black 'cut' #2A2925, not the logo grey #404040. The two greys are close enough to look like a mistake rather than a choice. The wordmark loses its logo blue #0070C0 and is set in the same near-black, so the blue is gone from the page entirely. The cause is the granite ground #B8B5AD, which sits in the logo blue's lightness band: the blue would fall below 3:1 on it. The tile fixes this by repainting the logo, when the rules allow only a different version of the logo (one the client approves) or a different ground.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo and its blue appear on his existing site and materials. He would no longer see his own mark here. The brief says the logo stays and is never redrawn, and his colours are open for him to rule on, not for the tile to quietly drop.

findings.where: Use of the accent colour, minium red: the hero headline 'MARK · M · MOSELEY / INFRASTRUCTURE · ADVISOR', the article heading, the 'CINZEL' specimen, the motion words 'LAID · WEIGHTY · SETTLED', the texture's 'M' and the easing curve, all next to the 'WRITE TO MARK' button
findings.fault: The direction claims 'one accent only, and it flows to the action', but minium has two jobs: every heading and the one button. On the first screen, the headline is a far bigger area of the same red than the button below it. The red therefore marks 'heading' more than 'act here', and the button is one red thing among several instead of the single figure.
findings.who_objects: A bank or agency visitor scanning for how to reach Mark: the eye goes to the big red name, not the red action. The layout round inherits a palette in which the action colour cannot be kept for actions.

findings.where: The palette as a whole, especially the article page specimen (Read mode) and its PDF link row
findings.fault: There is only one surface: the whole site, including long article pages, sits on mid-grey granite. Lime is barred from ever being a surface, and no lighter reading ground exists. Anything Angélique adds with its own white or light background will glare as a bright rectangle on the mid grey: a chart, a screenshot, a LinkedIn photo, a PDF cover. The palette gives no surface to hold such material.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, adding a post with a chart or a PDF thumbnail, and the reader of a long article. The brief requires every part of the look to survive a lay editor adding a post or a PDF.

findings.where: The style tile's section panels: 'Motion sketch' is boxed in a hairline frame, while 'An article page', 'Palette' and 'Type pair' sit open on the ground under the same heading rule
findings.fault: Sections of the same kind get different surface treatments. One is framed in a border inside its heading rule, and the others are not, so the tile does not show whether content blocks on this look take a frame.
findings.who_objects: The designer of the layout round, who must draw inside this look and cannot tell which is the rule for a content block: open on the ground, or framed.
